turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
My predicted top five are **c064, c005, c068, c017, and c073**. I prioritize close, high-performing training analogues and physically credible selective contacts over unfamiliar materials whose names alone do not establish good performance. These are predictions of configuration-level median efficiency, not measured rankings.

| Rank | Candidate | Training evidence and device-physics rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c064** | **TiO2-c / SnO2-np / MAPbI3 / Spiro-MeOTAD / Au.** The training set contains the same ETL with Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, and spin-coating followed by dipping at **20.85%**, plus TiO2-c / SnO2 with Spiro-MeOTAD and Ag at **17.47%** using spin-coating. The compact TiO2 provides electrode coverage and hole blocking, while the SnO2 overlayer offers a favorable electron-extraction interface. Spiro-MeOTAD/Au supplies a well-established hole-selective contact. I would not transfer the 20.85% result directly because both processing and metal differ, but this is a particularly strong candidate family. |
| **2** | **c005** | **TiO2-c / PCBM-60 / MAPbI3 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3 / Au.** Its closest training analogue—FTO, the same ETL, PCDTBT1, the same back contact, and the same two-step deposition—reaches **19.35%**. PCBM can improve electron selectivity and reduce recombination at the TiO2/perovskite interface; the polymer HTL and MoO3/Au provide a credible hole-extraction stack. The main uncertainty is the change from PCDTBT1 to PCDTBT8: polymer substitution can materially alter energetics, mobility, and coverage. |
| **3** | **c068** | **SnO2-np / TiO2-np / MAPbI3 / PTAA / Au \| MoO3.** The training configuration with ITO, SnO2-np, PTAA, and Ag reaches **18.19%**. Other SnO2/TiO2 combinations also perform well, including **16.54%** for SnO2-c / TiO2-c with Spiro-MeOTAD/Au. This candidate combines a credible electron-selective oxide stack with PTAA, a strong hole-selective material. Its performance depends on nanoparticle connectivity and absorber coverage; the additional TiO2 layer is not automatically beneficial. |
| **4** | **c017** | **C60-based electron contact with doped TaTm hole transport and co-evaporated absorber.** An almost identical training configuration, allowing for capitalization differences in material labels, gives **17.9%** with Au rather than Ag. This is unusually direct evidence. C60 provides electron selectivity, while F6-TCNNQ-doped TaTm supports conductive hole extraction. Co-evaporation can produce continuous films with controlled composition. Ag-contact chemistry is the principal difference from the training analogue. |
| **5** | **c073** | **TiO2-c / C60 / MAPbI3 / PTAA / Ag on an HMDS-modified ITO scaffold.** The corresponding ordinary-ITO configuration reaches **16.5%** in training. The TiO2/C60 combination offers electron extraction and interfacial passivation, paired with PTAA hole selectivity. The modified scaffold could improve coverage or contact geometry, although its wetting and added interfacial area introduce uncertainty. I select it because the underlying transport/contact combination is directly supported by the data, rather than assuming an unobserved additive must improve efficiency. |

The strongest uncertainty is the ordering within this group: the deposition labels omit important controls such as annealing, solvent treatment, layer thickness, and transport-layer doping. In particular, neither a favorable band alignment nor a passivating additive guarantees a low-defect, pinhole-free device.

Final: c064, c005, c068, c017, c073
